title: PageHeader
wrapsNative: navigationTitle(_:), navigationBarTitleDisplayMode(_:) on iOS, toolbar with ToolbarItem(placement: .primaryAction) and .secondaryAction, and a Menu for overflow actions
summary: The navigation bar is the page header: the title, the back button and the actions that apply to the whole screen. Status, details and section tabs sit below it as the first content. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: On every screen in a NavigationStack or NavigationSplitView.
whenNotToUse: For a heading inside a screen, use MonarchSectionHeader. For a screen that is not in a navigation container, such as a sheet with no navigation, put a title in the content with the header trait.

states.name: large title
states.description: The title is large at the top and collapses into the bar on scroll.

states.name: inline title
states.description: The title sits in the bar, for screens deeper in the hierarchy.

states.name: actions
states.description: The primary action sits at the trailing edge; secondary actions go into the overflow menu the system shows.

appearance: System navigation bar. Toolbar buttons take the theme's accent through the tint. Status badges, details and tabs below the bar are Monarch components in the content.
platformNotes: The web PageHeader draws the title, eyebrow, breadcrumbs, back link, status, details, tabs, a banner and an action row that overflows into a More menu below 640 pixels. On iOS the navigation bar owns the title, the back button (with the previous title) and the actions, and the system moves secondary actions into an overflow menu. Breadcrumbs and the eyebrow are not used: the back button and the navigation hierarchy replace them. Status, details, a banner and MonarchTabs are the first rows of the content. The web's sticky option is the default bar behaviour.
accessibility: System behaviour: the navigation title is the screen's heading and is read when the screen appears.
Toolbar buttons are buttons with 44-point touch targets and Large Content Viewer support.
The back button reads the previous screen's title.
edgeCases: navigationBarTitleDisplayMode is not available on macOS; the compiled example guards it with #if os(iOS).
Keep one primary action; more go into a Menu or secondaryAction placement.
Long titles truncate in the bar; keep them short and put the full name in the content.

examples.title: With breadcrumb, status and actions

parityExceptions.reason: The web puts New task and Share on the title row's trailing side; a phone column is too narrow for the title, the status badge and both buttons on one line, so the actions sit under the description in the same order (Share, then the primary New task). The title, status, breadcrumb, description and button tones are as on the web.
parityExceptions.convention: HIG: content wraps to the screen width instead of truncating
